guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C#'s hook is AfterPlayerTurnStart**Late**, a separate complete listener pass; the sim's on_player_turn_started is a single flat pass
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart runs three complete passes -- Early, then plain, then Late (Hook.cs:882-908) -- so a Late listener is guaranteed to see every plain listener's result. The sim's hooks.py has one walk per hook and no phase concept, which is audits/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G3 and audits/seam/turn_structure.json gap G12; one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, so this entry does not re-derive it. The Late phase is chosen here for a reason a HEAL cares about: running last means the 1 HP is added after any turn-start effect that costs HP, so it cannot be wasted against a full HP bar that a later effect then empties. DORMANT AT THIS SITE: the sim's on_player_turn_started relic listeners either damage enemies or grant block/energy, and the only ported turn-start effect that damages the PLAYER is relics/royal_poison.py -- which the sim also fires from on_player_turn_started, i.e. in the same flat pass, so the order between the two is registration-order luck and the HP total after both is 40 - 4 + 1 either way. It goes live for any pair where one member's amount depends on the other's result (a percentage-of-current-HP effect is the shape). Rule 7: Hook.cs, hooks.py and relics/royal_poison.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): the sim maps AfterPlayerTurnStart (step 22) onto on_player_turn_started, which the executed order puts at step 23 (AfterSideTurnStart)

Their effects (heal 1, gain 1 energy) do not interact. Porting a step-22 listener whose result a step-23 listener reads, or playing multiplayer where step 23 waits for other players, makes it live.
